bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Rockefeller Brothers Fund (RBF) was established in 1940 by the sons of John D. Rockefeller Jr. and Abby Aldrich Rockefeller: John D. 3rd, Nelson A., Laurance S., Winthrop, and David Rockefeller, as a vehicle for the members of their generation to systematically coordinate their philanthropic giving as well as share consultants, advice, and resources. Its endowment was created through a gift from JDR Jr. in 1951, and a subsequent bequest from his estate in 1960. Abby Rockefeller Mauzé, the eldest sibling and the only daughter of John D. Jr. and Abby Aldrich Rockefeller, joined the RBF Board in 1954.

John D. Rockefeller 3rd served as president of the Fund from its inception until 1956. Subsequent presidents in the 20th century included: Nelson A. Rockefeller, 1956-1958; Laurance S. Rockefeller, 1958-1968; Dana S. Creel, 1968-1975; William M. Dietel, 1975-1987; and Colin G. Campbell, 1998-2000.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The RBF Corporate Files consist of Board of Trustees meeting files, transcripts and records, Annual Reports and a variety of other publications including select papers and reports. The collection also includes administration, program and policy files, most notably from the Sustainable Development Program, and select files documenting Fellowships, the Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation, the Cults program, the Special Studies Project, the Water program and Westway. There is also a small selection of material documenting RBF interactions with governments, most notably the Ways and Means Committee of the the U.S. Government, and their activities pertaining to the regulation of foundations in the 1960s, and development of the bill that became the Tax Reform Act of 1969.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The Rockefeller Archive Center has title, copyright, and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them, and has authority to grant permission to cite and publish archival material from the collection.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Records 20 years old and older are open for research. All published materials are open for research.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Original order as received. Records are intellectually arranged in series, primarily by record type.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Administrative support files at Room 5600, primarily documenting the activities of the office when led by Arthur W. Packard. Administrative records include policy and procedure documents, memos, office manuals and guides, budget documents, declinations letters, and select personnel studies.
